newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen falls in grey trade on cooperation talks.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen falls in grey trade on cooperation talks.

text.p: Shares in German engineer Thyssen AG fell in unofficial trade after Fried. Krupp AG proposed cooperation talks with Thyssen after initially launching a 13.6 billion mark ($8.1 billion) takeover for the firm.

Brokers said the Thyssen share fell to around 413 marks in unofficial, or "grey", trade, having gone as high as 434 marks earlier on. Both shares were suspended from trade on announcement of the takeover bid.

In a compulsory statement on Wednesday morning Krupp said that it would discuss the possibility of setting up a joint steel company with Thyssen, which would replace the takeover bid if it was successful within eight days.
Brokers said that Krupp stood at around 300 marks in grey trade.
On Monday, the last day's trade for the two steel companies, Thyssen ended bourse trade at 346.80 marks, while Krupp ended bourse at 272 marks.
On Tuesday the smaller Krupp offered Thyssen shareholders a takeover price of 435 marks per share. Thyssen recommended that its shareholders not react to the offer for the time being.
